B: The open-hand banner, laid over the tomb like a blanket.
O: The tomb of King Osric Hale, carved with an open hand holding a sword by the blade.
"He kept the law. The law did not keep him."
L: The chaplain's account, sealed in wax. The seal has been broken and pressed back, many times.
"They say the king died of a broken heart. I was there. This is what I saw."
The candle gutters, and for a moment you are somewhere else.
A king's bedchamber, five hundred years ago. One candle. The queen's side of the bed, cold since she went missing.
King Osric lies awake. Downstairs, his war council waits for an order he cannot bring himself to give.
In the corner, the shadows thicken, and stand up, and become a man.
OSRIC: How did you get past the guards?
KALDOR: Second born. Second best. Second in line, my whole life. I would make the better king, Osric. Everyone knows it.
KALDOR: And at last, someone agrees with me.
Behind him, something that casts no shadow is listening. It has promised him power over the dead, and youth that never ends.
In the morning, the king sits up in his bed. His eyes do not blink. His hand moves slowly, as if someone else were moving it, and writes:
"Should I die, my brother Kaldor shall be king."
A month later, they rang the bells for King Osric. A broken heart, they said. A month is not very long. People talked.
Kaldor had it all: the gold, the fame, the queens. All on one condition. Build the strongest army in the eight kingdoms, and never march it to war. Defend, and only defend.
"I have told no one. Whoever reads this: forgive me. I was afraid."
The memory fades, and you are back in the cold of the crypt.
M: A small empty niche, labelled THE PRINCE. Never filled. They never found a body.
k: A candle. Somebody still tends it.
2: The stair back up to the chapel.
3: A short passage climbing to an iron gate. Grass on the other side, and sky.

objects.name: The Chaplain's Echo
lines: Ah. A light. It's been a very long time since anyone brought one down here.
Don't be frightened. I'm only what's left of someone who sat up too long beside a candle.
I keep it lit for him. Somebody should.

answer: I was the king's chaplain. I wrote down what I saw, sealed it, and didn't sleep for a very long time.
I don't need to now. It's restful, in its way.
He was a hard man, and at the end, not a well one. I prayed for him every night.
He also asked the bakers how the bread was. Both things are true. Most things are.
The boy's. They carved his name and waited for a body that never came.
So I stopped waiting for a body, and started waiting for a boy. It's a much nicer thing to wait for.

questions.ask: Keeping a candle for a mad king? Sad.
answer: Sad, yes. Most kind things are, a little.
* The candle gutters, then steadies. So does he.
